utterances.text: And then you settled your family?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we arrived at Niko Sakic's house, that is, in his basement, my family went to the shelter, and I stayed outside beside the house of Niko Sakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what side of the house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the side next to the road, next to the garage of Niko Sakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see there? Did you see your neighbours there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I saw Mirko Sakic; there was Dragan Samija; there was Miroslav Pudza; there was Milutin Vidovic. I don't know who else. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Niko Sakic anywhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was there the whole time. Sometimes he would go down to the shelter, and then he would be outside. He was around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see arriving then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Zume, I saw a group of soldiers arriving. They were well armed and in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did this group of soldiers look like? Can you describe them in greater detail?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you could see that they were a special group because they were well armed, their faces were painted, and they were wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone in a black uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were some who were in black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They all had automatic weapons, and they carried Zoljas on their backs, hand-held rocket launchers. I even saw RPGs, rocket-propelled grenades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The RPGs that they had, what kind of ammunition is used for that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they use missiles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you see them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were carrying them on their backs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your conclusion? What kind of unit was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I saw them. They had white belts, so I assumed it was some kind of military police by those belts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The regular army, the regular soldiers, are they armed like that? Do they have those kinds of weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, no; they only have one weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anybody from those units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I recognised the late Mirjan Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't have any paint on his face. His face was clean, so I could recognise him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know him well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him well. He's our neighbour. He lived in Santici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, in view of the fact that he was living in Santici, was he familiar with the terrain?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's not a large area. He would come often; he was in the warehouse often. He would come to Vlatko Kupreskic's warehouse often, and he knew the place. He moved around a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do in Vlatko Kupreskic's warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he would take the necessary food, foodstuffs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he went to the store; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether that shop, which was in Vlatko Kupreskic's warehouse, was the only shop that operated in those three villages of Santici, Pirici, and Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at that time, it was the only one that was working, so almost all the neighbours would come to the shop and buy the food that they needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did that unit go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after they passed, they came from the direction of Zume. They passed by Niko Sakic's garage, and they went in the direction of Vlatko Kupreskic's warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which unit Mirjan Santic belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that he was a member of a unit called Jokeri, Jokers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the Jokers had their headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, from stories, I knew that they were somewhere in the Bungalow, but I never saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see it because you didn't go there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I never passed along that road, so I didn't see that. I only heard that they were somewhere there in the Bungalow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps I would be happy to intervene. I think my learned friend has had a slip of the tongue. I think she might have meant a couple of questions back "Mirjan Santic." She said "Mirjan Kupreskic."

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No. I said "Mirjan Santic." I didn't say "Kupreskic." It can't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Well, then it's obviously been misrecorded, so we should put that right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It's a mistake, definitely.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, you said it right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: My colleagues tell me that I did say "Mirjan Santic." Thank you very much and thank you to my learned colleagues. Of course, I would like for that part of the transcript to be corrected, that this is Mirjan Santic as a member of the Jokers. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard that that unit was in the Bungalow. Did you hear anything else about that unit? Did you know who it belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I knew that they were part of the military police, if you can say that, but I had heard all of that. I didn't know anything exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please indicate on the aerial photograph where the unit came from, where did it go, and also the place where you saw them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from which direction did they come?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I was here, next to the garage of Niko Sakic (indicating), and the group of soldiers that I mentioned was coming from the direction of Zume, down towards the Modus warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point out on the photograph on the ELMO, could you put an arrow in the direction that they were going and could you mark the place where you saw them? Where did you see them approximately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm here, next to the garage, and they are going in the direction of the warehouse of Vlatko Kupreskic, warehouse Modus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This part that you marked, so this is the direction that we were moving along, next to the forest, is there a path there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There is a narrow path, a footpath. You can't drive along there in any kind of vehicle or cart, so it's only a footpath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there another path on the other side from the lower part of the forest that would lead from the Kupreskic houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to me, it seems like if it's from the upper side --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, from the upper side.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is. The road forks off. It goes right towards the Kupreskic houses, and then it also goes straight towards the Modus warehouse. There are two paths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they are both footpaths?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, only pedestrians can go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that group passed, also from the direction of Zume, Zoran and Mirjan came, and they also came to the garage. They came up to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they stay there, next to the garage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mirjan stayed, and Zoran, when he saw the refugees who were living in the Kupreskic houses, when he saw them coming out of the depression, he went with them in the direction of Zume. He took them to the same shelter where he took his family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did those refugees come from? Did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they came out from the depression, from the direction of the Kupreskic houses. They came out by Niko Sakic's garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they took this other footpath?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they took this other footpath that you asked about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did the gunfire begin? When did you hear the first gunfire, and what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At about 5.30, it could have been, you could hear strong gunfire from the direction of the Kupreskic houses, and at the same time, shooting also broke out from the direction of the road, from the direction of the Topole cemetery, the Croatian cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since the bullets really started flying -- and you could hear them breaking the branches, you could hear when a bullet breaks a branch -- so we escaped to the depression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to that depression? Why did you pick that place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the first reason is so that we could be close to the shelter, as much as we could, to protect our families that were in the shelter. And because of the configuration of the terrain, it was an ideal shelter -- not a shelter, but nothing could hit us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, did you stay in the depression?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were there the whole day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with you there that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After we ran into the depression, the people who were there, then two or three minutes later Zoran ran up from the direction of the house of Niko Sakic, so he ran there too. So Zoran Kupreskic was there, his brother Mirjan Kupreskic, Mirko Sakic, Dragan Samija, Miro Vidovic, and me, as far as I remember. I don't think I've forgotten anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Niko Sakic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He would run up to us occasionally, but at that time, we would also run out of the depression and go to the shelter to see what was happening with our family, and also for our parents to see us, because they were also worried that something might happen to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, us; Croats who were there in the depression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So who went to see their parents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That day, on two or three times, I left. Also Zoran and Mirjan did the same, and Mirko. When I say "we," I mean all of us who were there in the depression. So we took turns to go and see how our families were doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all those families in the same shelter?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, my family was in the shelter in Niko Sakic's house. Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic -- no, Mirjan Kupreskic's family was in the shelter in the house of Jozo Vrebac. Zoran's family was in the house of Milutin Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the family of Mirko Sakic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the family of Mirko Sakic was in the house of his father, Niko Sakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the family of Dragan Samija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were also in that same shelter in Niko Sakic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that day, that morning, on the first day, if anything else happened close to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. Sometime between 10.30 and 11.00, Nikola Omazic ran from the direction of Zoran Kupreskic's house. He said that Mirjan Santic had been killed, and that we need to come to the edge of the forest in order to help to move the body, to bring the body to the house of Niko Sakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mirjan Kupreskic, Zoran Kupreskic, and I went to the edge of the forest, and Ivica Kupreskic brought Mirjan Santic up there with Nikola and then we took the body over -- Zoran, Mirjan, myself, and Nikola, who had come up from there. So we took the body and took it to the garage of Niko Sakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he stay in the garage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Nikola Omazic went to tell his first cousin, who was the closest, the cousin of Mirjan Santic. His cousin was Milan Samija. Maybe his house was 200 to 250 metres away from the garage of Niko Sakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the house of Nikola Omazic? Is it close?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's not far. Maybe it's less than 300 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us if your family stayed in the shelter all day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sometime in the afternoon, at about 4 p.m., they left the shelter to go to the shelter of Niko Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did everybody from the shelter go or only your family?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, everybody from the shelter went to the shelter of Niko Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about you? Where did you stay?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I remained in the depression with the others who were with me the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I would like for us to look at a videotape of the depression, and this is a long tape. It's not too long. It's about 15 minutes. We tried to show the road that leads to the shelters, and then in certain sections we could speed it up, but our intention was for the Trial Chamber to get some kind of sense of how long it takes to go there, where it is situated in relation to the Kupreskic houses and to the shelter. So I would like to submit the translation of the text which will be on the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The videotape is marked D106/2, and the transcript is D106A/2. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Please, could we speed up this part, and we can come back later.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "In the village of Pirici, in the municipality of Vitez, we are in the place called Dolina. It is owned by Ivo Kupreskic. Near this place, Dolina, is a wood owned by my father, Stipan Vidovic. Dolina is situated precisely west from the houses of the Kupreskics, in the direction of the settlement of Zume. "From this place, Dolina, we are moving toward the Kupreskics' houses."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, whose houses are these here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the left-hand side we first come to Ivica Kupreskic's house, and then behind the pine tree we shall see the house of Ivo Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this farm exist in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, this was built later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose house is this on the right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is Ivo Kupreskic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not a stable; it's a house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's a house.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "We are now in front of the house of Branko Kupreskic, Josip Kupreskic, Ivica Kupreskic, and their father, Ivo Kupreskic. "To the east of the Kupreskic houses are Muslim houses. This is middle or central Ahmici, the central part of the village of Ahmici. "We are now in front of the house of Mirjan Kupreskic and Zoran Kupreskic. "This is the view from Zoran's house to Sakib's house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a pathway from Sakib's house to the house of Zoran Kupreskic through the depression?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "This is the view of Sakib Ahmic's house. "We are now at the house of Sakib Ahmic. This is the view from the house of Sakib Ahmic towards the house of Mirjan Kupreskic and Zoran Kupreskic. "The view from the house of Sakib Ahmic towards the house of Vlatko Kupreskic and the Modus warehouse. "We are now in front of the house of Josip Kupreskic, and beside it there is a garage. "We are now moving from the Kupreskic houses in the direction of the depression which is owned by Ivo Kupreskic."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are moving from the house of Ivo Kupreskic, which is the closest one to the depression?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Ivo Kupreskic's cowshed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's to the right. As we walk down the path, it's behind the farm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's lower than the farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The path you are taking is the path usually used to go from the houses of the Kupreskics' to Santic's house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "This is the depression we have mentioned, and we are now moving in the direction of the house of Niko Sakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the path leading through the depression?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "The house of Niko Sakic. We have now passed by the garage."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building that we saw before the house is the garage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is the way to where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To Zume. It has now been asphalted, so you could drive up to Niko's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose is the first house on the right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ilko Brnada.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the one on the right now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a crossroads?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, to the house of Nikola Omazic, and to Niko's house on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The houses we are passing by now are all these Croatian houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for now. Anto Pudza on the left, Milan Samija, and then 100 metres to the right there are a few Muslims' houses: Ramo Bilic, Zijad Bilic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Strmonja houses there next to the Bilic house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Miralem Strmonja, with his family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose houses are these?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side we see the Bilic house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ramo Bilic, Zijad Bilic, and his brother, who is in Austria, Miralem Strmonja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These houses have roofs with four sides?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the Croatian houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They had two-sided roofs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "We're now in front of Niko Vidovic's house, where the shelter was for civilians."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this shelter, was your family inside in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, from 4.00 p.m. Now we're going towards the house of Milutin Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this still the road leading towards the house of Jozo Vrebac and Milutin Vidovic, going through the Croatian part of the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it goes through the Croatian houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this still Santici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. This is Zume. We call this place Zume, but it is part of Santici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Now we can speed up this part, until we arrive at those two shelters. It's okay. We can stop here. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "We have now arrived at the house of Milutin Vidovic. We will now go from the house of Milutin Vidovic in the direction of the house of Jozo Vrebac."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the house across from the house which you say belongs to Jozo Vrebac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "We are now in front of the house of Jozo Vrebac." I couldn't hear. The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is the house across from the house of Jozo Vrebac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is, in fact, the shelter of Jozo Vrebac's son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his son-in-law's name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, he was from Macedonia. His name was Dragan. I don't know exactly what his second name was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in fact, the house across the road was the shelter, the yellow one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when this tape was made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was just before Christmas. It was on Christmas Eve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last year?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Last year, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Vidovic, can you tell us whether you stayed in that depression the second and the third day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The people I enumerated stayed there. We were all together there the second and the third day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Ivo Kupreskic's cowshed, which we saw on the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the cowshed underneath Ivo Kupreskic's farm building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the second and third day, were the same people you enumerated with you, the ones you said were there on the first day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were together all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go anywhere from Ahmici? Did your family move anywhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the second day, in fact -- yes, the second day of the conflict, in the evening, my family left Niko Vidovic's shelter and went to Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did they stay in Rovna, and who did they stay with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They stayed there a day or two, and they stayed with Zvonko Santic, who is my uncle, and that's why they went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, on the third day, what did you do and what happened to you on the third day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the third day, two military policemen arrived and took us to some kind of front line in Pirici, and that was the first time that we went up to the Muslim houses. We saw that they had been burnt down and that there had been victims, that there were dead Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When we passed by the house of Enver Sehic, we saw that his house had been burnt, and he was lying there dead with his son. I remember well Zoran cried then because they had been good friends, Enver and he. Then we saw the house of Hazrudin Ahmic and his father Munib Ahmic, and Zulejha Ahmic had also been burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which road did you take towards Pirici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there is a path there. We took a shortcut. We don't take the round way. We went through the fields. It was the closest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you stay at Pirici? Where were you told to go in Pirici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The first houses in Pirici, when we arrived there, we met for the first time Slavko Papic. He was the one who was deciding where people were going to dig in. Since I knew that he was an officer, a reserve officer in the old army, I assumed that he knew about these things and that that was the reason why he was entrusted with this duty. That's how it was, so we started to dig in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was taken to Pirici on that day, together with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was the whole group that was in the depression that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran and Mirjan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were there too. Mirko Sakic, Dragan Samija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you dig trenches there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did a little bit, even though we had no idea what kind of a trench we should be digging, but we dug a hole so that we could hide there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk with the military police who brought you up there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. About 20 metres before we reached the place where we stopped, one of those two said to us to guard that line well, and I quote him: "Because if the Muslims break through that line, they will do to you the same that we did to them."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those two military police members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that place, in Pirici, did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We stayed there that night. Then Slavko Papic came and told this group of ours to move to Gornji Ahmici. We were afraid, so we started to argue about that. We didn't want to go right away, but after a day or two, we had to go to the place where he sent us. We dug in there, and we stayed there until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I would like the following material to be admitted into evidence, 105 -- D105, 106, and 107/2. I'm sorry. I wasn't following the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And 107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: -- 106A. There's no 107.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The tape and the transcript. No objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. They are admitted into evidence. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are no -- I apologise. Counsel Puliselic will question the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Puliselic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to put one question to Mr. Vidovic. Examined by Mr. Puliselic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you are from Pirici, that you live in Pirici.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us if there is another person called Dragan Vidovic in Pirici, Santici, Ahmici, or in another place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In those places that you mentioned, at that time, there were six Dragan Vidovics. Right now, there are five because Dragan Vidovic from Buhine Kuce was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your father's name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Stipo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the names of the fathers of these other persons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Vidovic, son of Anto; Dragan Vidovic, son of Nikica; Dragan Vidovic or Drago Vidovic, son of Frano; Dragan Vidovic, son of Ivica; and Dragan Vidovic, who was killed at Buhine Kuce, his father's name was Anto.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were six people called Dragan Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Blaxill?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Blaxill:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I bid you good afternoon, Mr. Vidovic. My name is Michael Blaxill. I'm one of the Prosecuting attorneys assigned to this case. As a result of your testimony, I do have a number of questions I would like to ask you, sir. If we can go back to where you started your evidence in connection with the village guards, you indicated that this was a cooperative effort in the earlier part of 1992; is that correct? You cooperated, the Muslims and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if I understood you correctly, you indicated that each group of village guards operated very much close to home, in your own small part of the village or your own section of the village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We were close to our houses. We didn't venture further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For your participation in the village guard, let us say for the early part of 1992, before the first conflict for sure, could you just indicate on the big photograph the area that you patrolled with your colleagues, just roughly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We would go in this direction. There are these houses here, these houses here, and these Kupreskic houses up here (indicating). We didn't go further than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just remain for one moment. The Muslim guards who were operating in a similar area, could you just indicate if they covered any different parts of the village than yourselves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Muslim guards that I saw, that we were together with, would be here (indicating), in this section, from the main road up until Vlatko Kupreskic's house. We didn't go any further. I assumed that they watched -- that they had guard duty there and also in this section here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed. Perhaps you would care to sit down again, sir. Thank you. Now, initially, it sounds, from what you say, like there was little by way of any arms, that often the village guards, Muslim or Croat, were, in fact, patrolling without weapons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But then you were asked about an occasion, it was suggested to you that the Muslims became armed, but you mentioned something to do with a truck. Could you describe in a little more detail, sir, what you noticed about this truck, when and where you saw it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I noticed it in front of my house. Twenty metres away from me, this truck passed from the main road in the direction of Gornji Ahmici. It was a green truck driven by Muharem Pezer because I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the truck have any kind of identifying writing on it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a private truck, so on the door, there was the name of the owner of the truck. I couldn't read what it said, but I knew it was his truck. I know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us a description of the bodywork of the truck? Did it have low sides or high sides or can you describe that, the rear bodywork?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was a dump truck. It didn't have a tarpaulin, so I could see the weapons. I could see the crates with the ammunition. The truck, like I said, had two Muslims in it. One of them was holding an automatic weapon in his hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you refer to this as a dump truck. Would it be fair to describe, therefore, that the rear of this is like a big, deep bucket that would then tip? Is that the kind of bodywork that it had?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have a driver's license to drive trucks, so I know what a tipper is. Yes, it can rise up and dump the load.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just thinking, therefore, the rear portion is fairly deep, is it, because it has to carry loads and then it can tip them out, so it's a fairly deep container?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. The sides are, but the back flap is low, so I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying that your sighting of the load within this vehicle was, in fact, through the rear where the bodywork is low; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because the truck was coming from the direction of Ahmici, naturally, as it passed at a certain moment, it was in front of me, and then I could see the load from the back, but I also saw them holding it in their hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you standing at road level at that time, sir? In relation to the truck, were you at road level?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was that level. But since it was a little bit of a distance away, then I was able to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you actually have the opportunity to see into the rear of the truck?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps for 30 to 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated you saw boxes inside the truck; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember how many boxes you saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I don't remember. I saw boxes, grey-green, olive green. I knew they were military boxes, and I assumed that they contained ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. You assumed that a bunch of green boxes were military and contained ammunition; you didn't actually see ammunition as such, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I mentioned those boxes, but I didn't mention the ammunition. I just said that I saw the weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, to be perfectly accurate, what you're saying is you saw some boxes that appeared, from their shape and colour, to be military. That is what you actually saw; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I know that. I know they are military boxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the boxes not covered by a lid of some description?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see. I didn't see any other boxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct if I now say to you, sir, that your suggestion that you witnessed arming by the Muslims comes down to about 30 seconds of time in which you saw some military-looking boxes in the back of a lorry; is that what you're trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I say that I saw on the truck, on the flatbed, weapons, I can't say exactly how much, but automatic weapons, some PAP rifles. They are obviously different from the automatic rifles. Then for the boxes, I said that I assumed that they contained ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that that accounts for the boxes, but you also saw loose weapons, did you, in the back of this truck?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this brief sighting, you cannot, of course, say how many, because you didn't see them for long and you didn't have time to count, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we can move on to the later part of 1992, the village guard system is operating, and you've indicated that there were often problems or disputes over availability of people to perform their guard duty and that Mr. Zoran Kupreskic tried to resolve some of these difficulties; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did Mr. Kupreskic become, as it were, known amongst the guards as being the person who tried to sort out their schedule and arrange their duties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they knew one another very well, and, of course, they knew that he was doing those things, that he was trying to do something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, as a group, the village guards, have any particular contact or liaison with the civil defence members for the village area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that period, I don't know that anybody ever came to tell us something or to draw our attention to something in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicated that you, in a sense, took over this duty from Mr. Zoran Kupreskic. When did you take over from him, trying to handle these various administrative matters for the village guard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean when you say "administrative." What do you mean by that, "administrative"? It was just reaching an agreement. If somebody didn't come out on duty, somebody would complain, and then I would go to them to see why they didn't turn up. If this was a justified reason, I would say, "Well, you can then make this up the next time." So at the end of January. As you say, that was the duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took over this kind of task of trying to resolve difficulties; you say you took that over in January of 1993 or thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time. It's a convenient point, certainly subject matter-wise, to take a break if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. A 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaxill?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, if I can now move on to the slightly later part of 1992, you said that you had served for some time as a reserve police officer. Was that a civilian police organisation or was that a military type of police organisation that you had served in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was the civil police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you quit the police reserve, can you tell me when that was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that police, I served for two or three months, which would mean sometime around April or May, but I'm not sure exactly when it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would be 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes -- no, no. Sorry, sorry. '91.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: '91; sorry. Did you have any ongoing obligations to the police in the event of -- I don't know, civil unrest or anything like that for the future or was your severance from the police a permanent thing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was permanent. I left because I had to work, I had other duties, so, of course, I couldn't go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then, in fact, basically worked and were a civilian, you say, right up until, indeed, the start of the second conflict, in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if I can turn to what has been called the first conflict, which occurred, I understand, on the 20th of October, 1992, you say that the preceding day you had been to work as usual; is that so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you made reference to a village checkpoint that was set up by some Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when that was set up? Was it in fact set up on the 19th of October or had it been there the day before or do you recall when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was before. That roadblock was set up several days before that conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for several days you'd been going to and from work, and you had passed through that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I went to work, but I passed by that checkpoint for a few days before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just point on the large photograph, sir, could you point to where that checkpoint you refer to was positioned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was, as we said, on the road to Ahmici -- some 15 or 20 metres down the road, to be more precise -- near the cowshed of Sakib Ahmic, here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. If you would care to sit down again. I'm obliged for your help. Now, Mr. Vidovic, did you hear around the 19th of October of any other form of checkpoint or roadblock that had been set up in that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of any particular activity that may have occurred that day, the 19th, in the vicinity of the Catholic cemetery up on the main road, which I believe runs from Vitez towards Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That day, I didn't know anything, nor did I hear anything from anyone about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about a checkpoint or something of that nature up near the cemetery on the 20th of October, when there was the conflict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, on the 19th, I didn't know anything, but the next day, that is on the 20th, in the afternoon, I heard that there was a checkpoint and that that was actually where the conflict started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you establish, in the days prior to the 20th of October, the reason why the Muslim people had set up that smaller checkpoint on the road into Ahmici village? Did anyone explain to you why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. No one explained that to me, so I didn't know the reason why the checkpoint had been set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the people who were manning that checkpoint members of the Muslim village guard, to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, up to that point, still have any kind of joint cooperation or at least contact between Muslim and Croat village guards? Were you still talking to each other at that time, October '92?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we talked. Until the moment I mentioned, we even patrolled together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the course of this cooperative activity, did you or any of your colleagues raise the question of this checkpoint with your Muslim village guard counterparts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we kept watch together before this checkpoint was set up, and I didn't know they were going to set it up, or I would have asked why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, with respect, Mr. Vidovic, you as a village guard, did you see part of your duty as protecting the safety and interests of the Croat inhabitants within your area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, both the Croats and the Muslims, because that's why we were there, to protect the area we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when this checkpoint suddenly appeared and local citizens were being checked by these people, did you not think to query why this step had been taken by the group of Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There was no one I could ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you passed by that checkpoint for some days prior to the 20th of October, I believe you said you'd recognised the people on the checkpoint as being village guards; is that so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I presume, sir, they were people who were personally known to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have counted them at least as reasonably good acquaintances, if not friends of yours, prior to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it not have been a simple thing for you to ask them why they had taken this action?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after they would not allow us Croats entry into the primary school, I saw that they were making their relations with us more tense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you read this action as, in fact, a heightening of tension between Muslims and Croats within the community; is that so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after that, yes. Yes, that's how we could describe it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the village guard, you and your colleagues had, if you like, voluntarily assumed the duty of trying to protect the Croat citizens; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is there any other action that you took when you noticed this existence of a checkpoint run by the Muslims? Did you report it to anybody? Did you contact any form of authority about it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't contact anyone, nor did I know who I could contact to check why it was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to the 19th of October itself, I believe you said you saw 30 to 40 soldiers entering the primary school, I think, that evening; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the nature of their clothing? What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, some of them had camouflage uniforms and some of them were wearing civilian clothes, ordinary clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all these people armed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that each one of them carried a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell whether these people were Croat people or Muslim people, local people or from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since they arrived from the direction of Gornji, Upper Ahmici, I concluded that they were Muslims. But whether they were villagers, I couldn't see exactly who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of day was it when these soldiers arrived, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't daytime. It was at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So in fact it was too dark, was it, to be able to identify the individuals at all? You could just tell whether they were uniformed men or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't know their faces because, for example, I was about 50 metres away from the Modus warehouse where there was a light. So I saw the group, I saw how they were dressed, I saw their weapons, but I couldn't recognise their faces from that distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, from the 50-metre distance, sir, was the light inside the Modus warehouse, or is that light outside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was in front. The road was well lighted along which they passed, the group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I made a brief note, I hope accurately, that you felt suspicious. There was something suspicious about this arrival of 30 or more soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet you say you took absolutely no action to inform anybody about these men turning up at the primary school in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. I didn't inform anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, already, sir, you have said that in your role as a village guard, you have already witnessed the appearance of a Muslim checkpoint at the entry to the village, and now, late on the 19th of October, you witnessed 30 or more armed men arriving in the village, and you say you felt no need to inform anybody about this development?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't think it was necessary because up to the 20th, there had never been any incidents between the Muslims and the Croats. There had been no shooting, no killing, nothing that might lead me to the conclusion that something was being prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw these soldiers, you say you actually hid yourself so that you wouldn't be seen by them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at the end of the 19th of October, you presumably retired to bed, did you, sir, not thinking there could be any problem emanating from the Muslims in your area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've already heard in this Chamber from others that it was somewhere around 5.00, or a little after, in the morning that there were detonations heard, and people were woken up by it, and you were one of those. Is that right, sir? You were woken up by an explosion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the detonation at about 5.00 a.m., as I said, woke me up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that there was then an intensification of gunfire, small-arms fire, and you heard bullets obviously falling nearby to your home; yes, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The detonation was at about 5.00. After an hour or an hour and a half, I heard gunfire. I heard bullets falling onto the roof of my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you said that during the course of that day, essentially, you took some form of shelter in the depression; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After I had taken my family to the shelter, we went to the depression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have heard from one gentleman, who states he was in the depression, that there was indeed a Dragan Vidovic, son of Niko, Nikola; was that Dragan Vidovic present in the depression, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Dragance. That's what we called him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he present during that day in the depression along with the rest of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Only -- I saw him in the morning. Later, as the day went on, I didn't see him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that during that day, a certain of those amongst you would, in fact, leave briefly, maybe, or for a longer period, and then return to the depression? Did that happen at all during that day, the 20th of October?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did the same, as I said, I left from time to time. All those who had family in shelters would go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it seems that overnight on the night of the 20th of October, if I heard you correctly, sir, you in fact then stayed the night in a barn, Ivica Kupreskic's barn; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, not Ivica Kupreskic's, but his father's, Ivo Kupreskic's barn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's my fault, yes. Mr. Ivo Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that that building is on the similar level to the rest of the Kupreskic households, the Kupreskic houses? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's a little lower in relation to Ivo Kupreskic's houses. It's drawn back a little, and lower down, a little lower down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that building, however, vulnerable or would have been vulnerable if the bullets had still been flying around up there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, a bullet might have strayed in there, but we were ignorant of such things, so we went there to have a roof over our heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went there to put a roof over your heads. You say, sir, you were ignorant of such things, but in the event of the violence that broke out that day, you were all sufficiently wise to remove your families to appropriate shelters, and you did so, and they stayed there for the whole day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You showed sufficient wisdom at self-preservation to go into the depression, where you believed you would not be in the path of bullets that were flying around in the course of the conflict; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet when it comes to seeking your refuge at night, with respect, you appear to have chosen a place of less safety than the depression or one of the shelters within the houses of the village; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We went into the barn, as I said, to put a roof over our heads because we couldn't sleep in the depression. We didn't go to anyone's house. We couldn't because we were afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it seems that during that period, over the next day, a large number if not nearly all the local Muslims, in fact, moved out of Ahmici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I saw, not a large number, but I saw Muslims who had lived in Zume. I saw them passing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it then come to your knowledge that a large number of the local Muslims had moved out? Did people tell you that in the subsequent day or so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was told the next day that practically they left, they left the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the circumstances under which they returned? Because I do believe they returned about four days later; I believe you said that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I only remember -- yes, I said that three or four days later they came back. Later, I found out that the Croats had requested some four automatic rifles that the Muslims had confiscated at the roadblock which was there, like you said, at the Topole cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who on the part of the Croat community was involved in any kind of contact or negotiation to persuade the local Muslim population to return?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember about those meetings. I wasn't informed about that. I didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become aware, through personal friendships with anyone or anything of that nature, aware of the identities of the people who did attend the meetings and conduct any such negotiations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, I wasn't interested in that, so I didn't ask anybody about it, and nobody told me anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true to say, though, sir, that the Muslim population in the main did return to their homes? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the first conflict, everybody went back to their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have made reference to seeing numbers of soldiers -- I think you intimated Muslim soldiers -- who would come and gather from time to time by the school; do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You suggested these are people who had been going out to fight on a front line; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had heard that, and I saw them going somewhere. Of course they would be going to the front line, dressed like that and armed like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly that that would have been a front line against the Bosnian Serbs, against whom there had been fighting for some while? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those lines that the Muslims were going to were against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe it's a realm of life in which you have taken little interest, and please say so if that is the case, but we have heard in this Chamber that one of the considerable sources of tension between the Muslim and Croat communities later in 1992 was the indifference of the Muslim population to the -- what we've referred to as Serb aggression; in other words, they didn't want to fight, and they wouldn't fight, against the Serbs. Did you ever hear anything of that nature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. But I know that they went to fight against the Serbs because they went to those lines in Cekrcici and Visoko, and the Serbs were normally on the other side and the Muslims were on this side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Croat soldiers engaged in any of these areas against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Croats went on the other side, to Vlasic. As far as I know, that's where the line of defence was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've also heard that one of the major or, perhaps, the major cause of the conflict that occurred on the 20th of October '92 was because a Muslim roadblock tried to stop Croat HVO troops going through to the lines at Jajce to fight against the Serbs, and the HVO forcibly removed that roadblock. That's what the fighting was about. Did you hear that to be the cause of the conflict on the 20th of October?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later there was talk, something to that effect, that that was the reason for the barricade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, I'm trying to clarify that, sir. You are trying to say to us that, within Ahmici, you saw groups of Muslim soldiers who were going off to lines to fight against the Serbs. With respect, it is illogical that Croats and Muslims should fight over somebody going to the lines to fight a common enemy, and that is what you're suggesting.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, may I ask you just one more thing, I believe, on that subject, and then I can move forward. You say that after the fall of Jajce, that was when you personally bought a semi-automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you, in fact, just give me a month for that, sir? Was that at the end of '92 or the beginning of '93?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think that that was in November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us say that during November and into the beginning of 1993, December, January, your village guards were then carrying on their duties as they had before; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But at that time already, after the fall of Jajce, we had weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now we have two village guards, one Muslim, one Croat, and both are armed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But even if the atmosphere between the two is not working together as before, presumably you maintained a mutual respect and peaceful coexistence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe, by that point in January '93, you had taken over from Mr. Zoran Kupreskic as the kind of man who would try to sort out any problems for the Croat village guard; I believe you said that is so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the end of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So relations remained peaceful, did they not, right up until April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we had no more incidents, no more checkpoints, no more problems; that is clear?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the general problem of tensions between the communities, did you have any form of line of communication established so that you could report any incident to somebody?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't have anybody to report to, nor did we know. We didn't know if anybody existed whom we could inform. So we would go on guard duty, and we were guarding our homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect, Mr. Vidovic, it does seem curious that you would operate in a vacuum. I mean, what would you have done if something had happened? Let's say that some soldiers had come out of the night while you were on guard duty and you would have found the community under attack; what steps could you have taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If something like that happened, an incident, we would have called the civilian police, and then at the time, we thought that they would deal with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were these civilian police located? Where would you have had to call them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Vitez, the security station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe by that time though, the HVO had been in existence for some considerable time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know. Well, I had heard stories that there was an HVO. I don't know. I wasn't a member, and I wasn't interested in that. I was just doing my work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I believe, sir, your place of work, was that in Vitez, if you perhaps just refresh my memory. I may be wrong.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Weren't you aware at the time, early '93, that effectively the administrative control of the municipality was in the hands of the HVO, that there was an HVO military as well? Did you not know this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I only heard about that. I didn't know exactly what it meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, like any citizen, you were aware of these things and aware of these names?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you were faced with that situation, it would not have occurred to you then to contact or have contact with the HVO, as the power in the area, to protect the citizens?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. As I said, if there were any incident, we would call the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will be speaking in greater detail about it in a moment, the early morning meeting that occurred on the morning of the 16th of April, but do you recall any civilian police representatives being present at that meeting at the house of Jozo Livancic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. There was no civilian police there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, as we get into April of 1993, we reach the day of the 15th of April. Did you, as a local resident, have any idea that there would be any kind of violence in your area in the near future?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. I couldn't even think about something like that. I thought that that would be resolved in a peaceful way. There could be some small things that would happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you had no feelings on the 15th of April, 1993 that you had to take any protective measures for your family or anything of that nature. It was a nice, normal day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could say that, for me, that day was like that. I went to work, like I said, and, of course, I worked all day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably, you went to bed the night before, i.e., the night of the 15th to the 16th, and you say you were later awoken by a telephone call. Could you just confirm for me again, sir, please, the time that you recall receiving that telephone call?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was about 2.30 to 3.00 approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying the telephone call to you was at about 02.30 to 03.00 in the morning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you stated it was the voice of the late Nenad Santic requesting you to go to the house of Jozo Livancic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any HVO connections or authority that may have been vested in Mr. Nenad Santic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know from the HVO. I knew that he was a member of the HDZ, Nenad Santic, and that he had a lot of information and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you received this request from Mr. Santic to go to the house of Livancic, did you ask him why at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, he told me, "There are some problems," and to go down there, for him to explain what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand or have any knowledge at that time as to why you had been chosen to receive such a telephone call?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, because in January of '93, they elected me as a member of the civil defence, so I was the person who supplied the civilians, the inhabitants, in the area where I was living.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the people who performed this election? Who were they who had the power to elect you to the civil defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I only know that Ivica Vidovic, Jevco, came and talked with me, and they thought that I was appropriate for this, that I could perform this duty. He asked me if I would agree to that, and, naturally, I did agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that, in reality, for the word "they," we should take it as meaning Jevco, Mr. Ivica Vidovic, is that right, if I'm saying the word right, "Jevco"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Jevco.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall what time you arrived at the house of Jozo Livancic on the morning of the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what time it was, but I think it was a little bit after 3.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have given us a list of the persons who were present. If I may just run through them to see that the list we have, that it is everybody, or whether there is anybody else. There was Mr. Jozo Livancic himself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jelko Livancic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That gentleman, Jelko Livancic, was that the son of Mr. Jozo Livancic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Jelko Livancic is the son of Jozo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same young man who sadly died in combat a few days later?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that he was in a battle line in Kuber when that occurred; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later, I heard that he was killed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of what his military unit or his military role was when you saw him on the night of the 16th, young Mr. Jelko Livancic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that he belonged to any unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he, in fact, wearing, Jelko Livancic, when you arrived at the house? Was he in some sort of uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not certain because it seems that he had a camouflage uniform, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mr. Jozo Livancic? Was he wearing some sort of uniform or was he in civilian clothes or night clothing? What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was in civilian clothes. I didn't pay attention to that at the time, so I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Nenad Santic was also present; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he dressed in civilian clothes or was he dressed in some form or part of a uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, he had just a jacket, but again, I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By saying "just a jacket," do you mean that the only uniform he was wearing was a camouflage jacket or you're saying it was just a civilian jacket? Can you clarify that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was a camouflage jacket, but I'm not certain about it. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Others present at this meeting were also Mr., I think it's, Anto Kovic or Covic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Covic. Covic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then a Mr. Ivo Vidovic, Mr. Simo Vidovic, and Ivica Vidovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Simo Vidovic, as far as I can remember, I didn't mention Ivo Vidovic. Ivica Vidovic, Jevco.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think actually it may be my bad writing. Vujovic, Ivo Vujovic, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
