utterances.text: It's my fault. It's my poor handwriting. What about the way those people were dressed? Were they, again, in civilian clothing or were they in military attire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think they were in civilian clothes. They were elderly people. Again, that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that essentially the talking was done here by Jevco, Mr. Ivica Vidovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if any contribution was made by Mr. Nenad Santic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I heard that night in the house of Jozo Livancic, I heard it all from Jevco, that is, from Ivica Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you just try and think back as carefully as you can and tell us as precisely as you can what information you were given? What was it that you were told?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Jevco, that is, Ivica Vidovic, said that he had information that the Muslims might attack the Croats, that I should therefore go and tell Niko Sakic about this, and that I should take my household members and the neighbours to a shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given any information at all about when they thought this might take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no other information was given to us by him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall at what time you received this information? What time was it now? You arrived there at about 3.00. What sort of time do you have now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, I arrived there after 3.00, maybe ten minutes past three, a quarter of an hour past three, and then it might have been about half past four (sic) or twenty to four approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were you actually told this information shortly after arriving? I'm just trying to work out -- I don't quite understand the recorded reply, sir. I'm sorry. You say at ten or a quarter past three is when, what, you might have arrived or when you first heard this information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived, that's what I said. I arrived there at about ten past three. Then we sat down, and he told us that, and it might have lasted for -- well, it might have lasted until half past three, something like that, or forty minutes past three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After receiving that information, you were given the instructions to do your civil defence duty and warn people and get them to shelters; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given any additional information as to the direction from which any supposed attack would come?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't tell us that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've already said, and therefore I apologise if we're repeating ourselves, I think you said that you weren't given any idea of what time this attack was expected or feared; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I don't mean to repeat. I missed it. You've received this information; it is now something like 3.30 to 3.40 in the morning. What time did you eventually leave the house of Jozo Livancic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, about twenty minutes to four, I think it could have been around that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From there, where did you go first?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Jevco had told me to go to Niko Sakic's house because he was supposed to attend the meeting, but he wasn't informed, so he didn't come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I suggest going back to the persons who were present at the meeting. Do you recall whether you saw any of them again in the course of the 16th of April? Did you encounter them any place else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is just one thing I would like to return to for a moment, again, in respect of the unfortunate young man Jelko Livancic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I wonder if we could just make reference, Your Honours, to Exhibit D39/2. I don't think it's a document that necessarily will be recognised by the witness as such, but I will ask him just to look at one name in it. It is, I understand, a list of HVO casualties, deceased. I wonder if that could just be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, you see a document before you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I appreciate, sir, you are not the author of the document, but does that appear to you, on its face, to be a list of deceased soldiers working for an HVO formation? It looks like the Viteska Brigade. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I look at this list, when I read these names, I cannot conclude. But I see here Jelko Livancic, son of Jozo, under number 8, and it's true that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I said to you that a witness having put forward this very same information suggested that Mr. Jelko Livancic was, in fact, in the military police, would that in any way ring a bell with you or is that simply information you do not have?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that Jelko Livancic was in the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I just wanted to clear the point with you. We're obliged for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it would seem then, just one other factor, that at that point, when you left the meeting, Mr. Jelko Livancic was most assuredly in -- well, I'm saying the Ahmici region -- he was at the house of his father at that time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is, I believe, fairly close by, however, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not so close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away would you say that house was from Ahmici as a village area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you from my house, for example, a kilometre and a half to two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your house to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. From my house to the house of Jelko Livancic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the house actually appear on the large photograph? Can you identify the Livancic household? Or is it not on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I can have a look. It's here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed, sir. Thank you. So when you went -- please, do sit down, Mr. Vidovic. Thank you for your help. When you went to the house of Mr. Sakic, how long did it take you to get from the house of Livancic to Mr. Niko Sakic's house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, since it was night-time, it took me about 15 minutes or 20 minutes. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I imagine, sir, you were on foot at the time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you arrived at the house of Mr. Niko Sakic, and --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- how long did you remain at that house in order to advise him what to do and then -- before moving on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, well, if it took me about 20 minutes to reach his house, I arrived at about 4.00. I stayed there briefly. Two, three, four minutes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that house, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then I went to Ivica Kupreskic's house and Zoran Kupreskic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would have taken you how long? Two or three minutes to get there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you couldn't really get there in two or three minutes. Maybe five or six because there was a depression, it was dark, the road is not good. So five to six minutes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be true to say that you had alerted members of the Kupreskic family by about 15 to 20 minutes after 4.00 that morning? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe a quarter past four, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the various Kupreskic households, where did you then go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I had awakened Ivica and Zoran Kupreskic and explained things to them, I went to my house to wake up my parents, my wife, my children, and my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at what time did you reach your own home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, around about half past four, 20 to 5.00, approximately. As I said, all this is approximate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, it appears that your first call was to Mr. Niko Sakic because he obviously had not been contacted, and he too had civil defence duties to perform. Was the Kupreskic family part of your list of people to warn, particularly, and to relocate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They belonged to the people I was supposed to alert in such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from that location it was quicker to go straight to the Kupreskics', was it, rather than go straight to your own home? You could perform that duty quickly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, since it was my duty to wake them up, and it was along the way, of course, I woke up the two of them and told them to wake up the others in their homes, and then I would continue on my way to my house and to my other neighbours'.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Blaxill --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Yes, I was just--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Do you want to continue for one to two minutes, or shall we stop here?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I doubt the one or two minutes will do a great deal either way, Your Honours. It's a good break point in the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good. Thank you. So we will continue on Monday. May I remind you that on Monday we will be sitting from 9.00 to 1.00, and then from 2.30 to 5:30 on Monday. All right. So we adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
